lesson.title: Will it fold into a cube?
lesson.subtitle: P4 nets revision
lesson.objective: Tell which flat patterns of squares fold into a cube, and say why another does not.
lesson.story: Four flat patterns of squares are labelled A to D.

steps.title: Count the faces
steps.prompt: How many squares are needed to make a net of a cube?
hints: Picture a dice or a box shaped like a cube. Think about its flat sides.
Count the top, the bottom and the sides.
There are 4 sides, a top and a bottom.
A cube has 6 faces, so its net needs 6 squares. Enter 6.

steps.title: Pick the net that folds
steps.prompt: Which of the four patterns folds up into a cube, with no gaps and no overlaps?
hints: Imagine folding each pattern in turn. Keep one square still as the floor.
Fold the squares next to the floor up to make walls. Watch where each square lands.
Look for the pattern where every square lands on a different face. Rule out the others one at a time.
Net B folds into a cube. Choose Net B.

steps.title: Say why another does not
steps.prompt: Net A does not fold into a cube. Why not?

choices.label: The squares need to be turned round before the net can fold.
Two squares would land on one face, leaving another face empty.
There are not enough squares, so the cube would have a hole.

hints: Count the squares in Net A.
Imagine folding Net A. Follow where the squares go.
Look for two squares that would end up on the same face of the cube.
Choose: Two squares would land on one face, leaving another face empty.

steps.title: Explain your thinking
steps.prompt: What must be true for six joined squares to fold into a cube?

choices.label: Any six squares joined edge to edge will fold up into a cube.
Each square must land on a different face of the cube, with no overlaps.
The six squares must include a straight row of four squares somewhere.

hints: Think about the cube you would make.
Some six-square patterns fold and some do not.
A row of four is common, but not every cube net has one.
Choose the explanation about each square landing on a different face.
